question_text:
The following tabulated data were gathered from a series of Charpy impact tests on a tempered 4340 steel alloy.

| Temperature $\left({ }^{\circ} \mathbf{C}\right)$ | Impact Energy $(\boldsymbol{J})$ |
| :--: | :--: |
| 0 | 105 |
| -25 | 104 |
| -50 | 103 |
| -75 | 97 |
| -100 | 63 |
| -113 | 40 |
| -125 | 34 |
| -150 | 28 |
| -175 | 25 |
| -200 | 24 |

(a) Determine a ductile-to-brittle transition temperature as the temperature corresponding to the average of the maximum and minimum impact energies.
(b) Determine a ductile-to-brittle transition temperature as the temperature at which the impact energy is 50 J .

Give your answer as a tuple (answer to (a), answer to (b)).The units of each required answer are (°C, °C), respectively.
response:
## Reasoning

**Data:**
| T (°C) | 0 | −25 | −50 | −75 | −100 | −113 | −125 | −150 | −175 | −200 |
| E (J) | 105 | 104 | 103 | 97 | 63 | 40 | 34 | 28 | 25 | 24 |

### (a) Transition temperature at average of max and min impact energies

- Maximum impact energy = 105 J (at 0 °C)
- Minimum impact energy = 24 J (at −200 °C)
- Average = (105 + 24)/2 = **64.5 J**

The energy 64.5 J falls between T = −100 °C (63 J) and T = −75 °C (97 J). Linear interpolation:

$$T = -100 + \frac{64.5 - 63}{97 - 63}(−75 −(−100)) = -100 + \frac{1.5}{34}(25) \approx -98.9\ ^\circ\text{C}$$

### (b) Transition temperature at 50 J

The energy 50 J falls between T = −113 °C (40 J) and T = −100 °C (63 J). Linear interpolation:

$$T = -113 + \frac{50 - 40}{63 - 40}(−100 −(−113)) = -113 + \frac{10}{23}(13) \approx -107.3\ ^\circ\text{C}$$

$$\boxed{(-98.9,\ -107.3)}$$
